Step 9 complete.

## Adjudication: `confirmed_fatal`, both lanes, `dependency_citation`

The 8b/8c test comes out **the 8b way**. At 8c I refuted the objection because the item discharged the missing hypothesis from its own `[given]` and wrote the inference out. Here `[given]` supplies only ℝ(t) as fractions of ℝ[t], the equality criterion, the set *P*, and the `lc` notation — none of the four propositions `[L2]` asserts — and the Verification never writes the eventual-sign inference out. Old step 1.1 just asserted the sign and pointed at `[L2, L3]`.

Read on disk, `[L2]` asserts four things and cites three items that state none of them:

| conjunct | status |
|---|---|
| finitely many real roots | library *has* it (`thm-root-bound-for-polynomials-over-a-domain`, page 52) — not cited, not in `deps` |
| eventual sign = sign of lc | **nowhere in the library.** The order-9 counterexample derives it inside its *proof step 1.1*, but that's a step, not a proposition |
| ℝ[t] is an integral domain | stated by `cor-rational-function-field-as-a-fraction-field`, which is already in `deps` — `[L2]` just didn't cite it (Terra spotted this exactly) |
| lc(pq)=lc(p)lc(q) | stated by `thm-polynomial-degree-of-a-product-over-a-domain` — in neither `[L2]` nor `deps` |

I also found a second defect in the same sentence: "beyond all of them" is ambiguous, and on the reading "off the root set" it's **false** — p(t)=t has lc 1>0 and p(x)<0 for x<0.

## Repair applied, inside the delegation

- `[L2]` re-cited so every clause quotes a published Statement; new `[L6]` for absolute value.
- The eventual sign **stops being a Fact and becomes a proved step** — a new step 1.1 with an explicit threshold, five lines of ordered-field arithmetic (delegation route (b), written out in the repair record).
- That threshold gives "p(x)≠0 for x>X_p" for free, so the root-count conjunct is no longer needed and I deliberately did *not* add that dependency — smallest correction.
- `deps` gains four ids on pages 9 and 52, loses none; nothing renamed, deleted, or reordered.

All four escalation tripwires checked and clear: no new theorem or item (the natural alternative — a new lemma on page 52 — would have been both a new item and a reading-order change, which is why I didn't take it), no debatable restatement, no deletion, no reading-order change, no open impact queue.

Gates: precheck PASS with no REPAIR output, fwdcheck/extcheck/citecheck/rendercheck/prosecheck OK, `impact-audit` exit 0 with both consumers dispositioned (`cex-q-not-dense` still-licensed — its two cited conclusions survive verbatim as steps 3.2 and 4.1; `ex-cauchy-complete-not-complete-field` not-load-bearing, a Remark mention). depcheck's single remaining error is `published-unaudited` on this item.

## Answer to the explicit question

**Not yet safe to carry a verification stamp, and not from me.** The mathematics is now sound, but no author certifies its own repair — `verification.verified` (`scope: published-dependency-repair`, `delegated_by: owner`) must come from an independent Sol reader, and I deliberately did not write it. It does **not** need to go to the owner unrepaired.

Owed next: an independent certifier on the repair, and a paired rejudge with `--items ex-rational-function-field-order` (post-repair `item_sha256` `ab3f55bf…`; page-mates unchanged and spared).

Artifacts: `research/frontier-12-alpha-step9.md`, `research/frontier-12-published-dependency-repairs.md` §R1, `research/frontier-12-step9-impact.json`, two rows in `research/frontier-12-judge-adjudications.jsonl` against the pre-edit hash `3f0f776e…`.

One thing outside my scope, recorded not acted on: depcheck warns `cited-not-in-deps` on `cex-ordered-field-not-archimedean` — its `Given:` cites the fraction-field corollary, which the wiring put in `forward_refs` rather than `deps`. That's by design and fwdcheck passes, but it belongs in the wiring certifier's report.

Sources consulted for corroboration (not load-bearing): [Wikipedia — Polynomial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polynomial), [Lumen Learning — End behavior of polynomial functions](https://courses.lumenlearning.com/odessa-collegealgebra/chapter/use-the-degree-and-leading-coefficient-to-describe-end-behavior-of-polynomial-functions/).
